events_chronological: At an airport arrivals gate strangers greet the people they love, and a voice remarks that love is in fact everywhere.
A newly elected prime minister meets a young woman who works in the household at his official residence.
An ageing rocker records a festive version of an old hit and tells every interviewer it is rubbish.
A woman marries her fiance, and his closest friend films the whole wedding.
A widower buries his wife and cannot get his stepson to speak to him at all.
A writer finds his girlfriend in bed with his brother and goes abroad to work alone.
The head of a design agency finds that his new secretary is paying him a great deal of attention.
The agency head's wife runs a household around her daughter's part in a school nativity play.
A woman at the agency has loved a colleague for years and is interrupted every time by calls from her ill brother.
The stepson admits he is in love with a girl at school, and the widower is relieved that it is only that.
The writer and his foreign housekeeper fall in love without a word of shared language.
The friend shows the bride his wedding footage, which turns out to be entirely of her, and later stands at her door with a stack of cue cards.
A visiting head of state makes a pass at the young woman, and the prime minister denounces him at the press conference.
The agency head buys his secretary a necklace, and his wife finds it, assumes it is for her, and is given a compact disc instead.
The woman from the agency takes her colleague home, and leaves the bed to answer her brother's call.
The rocker's record goes to number one and he spends the holiday with his manager rather than at a party.
The writer flies south and proposes in front of an entire street, the prime minister finds the young woman backstage at the nativity play, and the widower takes his stepson through airport security.
Five weeks on everyone arrives at the same airport, and the telling closes on the gate it opened at.
nonlinear_category_reason: Every strand keeps its own forward order and nothing is ever shown out of turn in time; the inversions are only between strands running at the same moment, which the telling cuts between sideways. Nine strands run concurrently through the five weeks before Christmas, bracketed by the same airport arrivals gate.
syuzhet_notes: Nine loosely linked stories run concurrently through the weeks before the holiday, cut between constantly and joined only by a handful of shared characters. The telling never goes back in time.
fabula_notes: The five weeks are continuous and marked by a countdown. Strands that are simultaneous can be ranked either way.

events.content: At the arrivals rail, embraces among strangers turn an ordinary terminal into a visual claim that affection is everywhere.

reader: the airport will frame all of the separate love stories

prime minister: the household aide is candid and appealing

events.content: The same arrivals hall now contains the people from the separate strands, their altered relationships visible in greetings rather than narration.
